record.what_it_does: AI customer service platform that organizes support conversations around people, not tickets.
record.auth_notes: The docs say "Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication." Each API token belongs to a Gladly user, and that user needs the API User permission. An administrator grants this permission agent by agent under Settings > Users. Tokens are created under More settings > API Tokens > Create Token and are shown only once. Credentials go in the Authorization header as the agent email plus the token. A token can perform any API request without restriction, so there are no scopes. The docs do not mention OAuth. Requests go to each customer's own subdomain, {org}.gladly.com.
record.access_notes: Gladly's pricing page (gladly.com now redirects to gladly.ai) lists no plans or prices. It offers only "Get a Demo" and "Contact sales". There is no free tier, trial or self-serve signup. API tokens exist only inside a provisioned customer organization, and an admin must grant the API User permission. A developer cannot get credentials alone. Gladly says it will enable the API in a separate sandbox environment, which also appears to be provisioned through Gladly.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST reference lists 21 resource groups: Agents, Public Answer, Answer Management, Audiences, Business Hours, Communications, Conversations, Customers, Endpoints, Events, Export, Freeform Topics, Inboxes, Organization, Proactive Conversations, Reports, Tasks, Teams, User Identity, Topics and Webhooks. There is also a Lookup API. Operations were not counted exactly, but the total is likely more than 50. StackOne's third-party connector exposes 65 actions. An OpenAPI specification can be downloaded from the reference page.
record.mcp_notes: I found no official Gladly MCP server. Gladly's site, developer docs and search results show no first-party announcement. Third-party hosted servers exist from StackOne (https://www.stackone.com/connectors/gladly/mcp/) and Truto.
record.blocker_notes: The API is broad, documented and has an OpenAPI spec, so a toolkit is technically simple. It would use Basic auth with the org subdomain, agent email and API token. However, there is no free or trial account, and getting a Gladly organization or sandbox to build and test against requires going through Gladly sales or a partnership. There is no OAuth either, so end users must paste unscoped, full-access tokens. Customers who already use Gladly could connect their own tokens.
